Guidance & outlook: Against this, we are raising our EBITDA margin guidance to about 27% from the 25% to 26% we had guided in May.
Technology and Payments segment, which was 7% of our services revenue in FY22, has grown to 16% in FY26, is 18% in this quarter, and we expect this to cross 20% contribution by the end of Q4.
FY26 capex was around INR350 crores and the guidance for FY27 is around INR100 crores to INR125 crores.
Growth & demand: This is some modest growth on Q4, but is INR25 crores short of what we aimed for.
As of today, the currency fulfillment has recovered partially through Q2 to about 80% of indented volume.
Combined, the services revenue growth should be in the 15% to 19% range.
Margins & costs: In this environment, we delivered our highest ever services revenue and expanded margins by 170 basis points, while carrying higher -than-normal wage and fuel inflation in the cost base.
On the cost side, this year has seen very steep increases in state-level minimum wages, ranging from 6% to as much as 60% in certain key large states.
EBITDA came in at INR173 crores, up 8.9% on a year -on-year basis and 6.8% sequentially, with margin expanding 170 basis points quarter -on-quarter to 27.2%.
Capex & expansion: We are maintaining our increased spend on tech at 1.5% of revenue, so this margin expansion comes after fully carrying that investment.
For reference, FY26 saw peak capex of INR350 crores as against our average capex run rate of INR200 crores.
For FY27, we currently estimate capex to be substantially lower at INR100 CMS Info Systems Limited August 11, 2026 crores to INR125 crores range.
Balance sheet & cash: This is a risk we had called out in our May call, and this INR25 crores revenue loss has an operating deleverage impact on the P&L.
Now this has a direct impact on the operating deleverage for us on 12% of our revenue base.
As you are aware, we completed a share buyback on June 19, 2026, for 49.39 lakh shares at INR340 per share, totaling to INR168 crores.
Risks & challenges: Starting with currency, we normally see some disruptions around election cycles.
Similarly, there are other banks also evaluating o ur ALGO MVS software, which is a multi-vendor software for powering their ATM networks.
The competition is broadening as attractive markets will a ttract newer entrants.
